newsitem.title: USA: ANR says U.S. Gulf gas flows almost normal.
newsitem.headline: ANR says U.S. Gulf gas flows almost normal.

text.p: ANR Pipeline Co, a unit of Coastal Corp, said Tuesday that most of the natural gas shut in by producers on its southeast mainline as a precaution against Tropical Storm Josephine has been restored.
"We're pretty much back to normal on our southeast mainline," a company spokesman said.
He said about 400-450 million cubic feet per day had been lost on the system that included HIOS (High Island Offshore System) off Texas and Eugene Island Block 188 off Louisiana.
The spokesman said the system was flowing about 1.1 billion cubic feet per day (bcfd) this morning versus about 1.3 bcfd prior to the storm.

Josephine was downgraded overnight from a tropical storm as it dissipated when it moved across Florida. At 0500 EDT, the storm was 50 miles southeast of Savannah, Georgia, moving east-northeast at 25 mph, with winds of about 50 mph.
